RAJYA  SABHA
————
List of Questions for ORAL  ANSWERS
to be asked at a sitting of the Rajya Sabha to be held on
Friday,  the July 29, 2005/Sravana 7, 1927 (Saka)

(Ministries: Agriculture; Chemicals and Fertilizers; Consumer Affairs,
Food and Public Distribution; Environment and Forests; Food Processing
Industries; Health and Family Welfare; Railways; Steel)
Total number of questions — 20
Benefits of Support Price Policy to
small land holders
†*81. SHRI RAJ MOHINDER
SINGH MAJITHA:
SHRI RAVI SHANKAR
PRASAD:
Will the Minister of AGRICULTURE
be pleased to state:
(a) whether it is a fact that there are
around 89.35 million families which are
associated with agriculture in the
country;
(b) if not, Government's assessment
thereof and whether it is also a fact that
out of these, 66 per cent families are
having one hectare or lesser agriculture
land only;
(c) if not, the facts in this regard;
(d) whether it is also a fact that small
land holders in the country are not getting
any benefit from the ongoing support price
policy of Government; and
(e) if so, the reaction of Government
thereto and the scheme formulated by
Government to make the land of farmers
belonging to the said group, beneficial?
Sale of tickets through mobile vans
†*82. DR. CHHATTRAPAL SINGH
LODHA:
PROF. R.B.S. VARMA:
Will the Minister of RAILWAYS be
pleased to state:
(a) whether it is a fact that Government
are going to formulate a plan to sell rail-
tickets through mobile vans;
(b) if so, the details of the plan; and
(c) by when the scheme is likely to be
launched?
Rail accidents
*83. SHRI DATTA MEGHE: Will the
Minister of RAILWAYS be pleased to
state:
(a) the details of rail accidents occurred
in various parts of the country during the
last three years, year-wise;
(b) the number of persons killed and
injured in these rail accidents;
(c) whether the causes of these rail
accidents have since been inquired into;
(d) if so, the particulars of railway

personnel who have so far been held
responsible for these rail accidents;
(e) the action so far taken against these
railway personnel;
(f) whether any progress  has so far
been made in installing Anti-Collision
Device (ACD) in trains; and
(g) if so, the details thereof?
AIDS patients
*84. SHRI S.S. AHLUWALIA: Will the
Minister of HEALTH AND FAMILY
WELFARE be pleased to state:
(a) the number of AIDS/HIV affected
patients, State-wise in the year 2000;
(b) the number of new cases registered,
year-wise thereafter till 31st May, 2005;
(c) the details of special drive
undertaken, if any, for ascertaining their
numbers as well as identifying the affected
persons who might be avoiding to come to
Government health centres;
(d) the details of NGOs engaged in
combating AIDS;
(e) the funds allocated to each, year-
wise since 2000-01;
(f) whether a phenomenal change in the
number of HIV /AIDS affected persons
was observed in the recent past; and
(g) if so, what could it be attributed to?
Shortage of wheat stock
*85. SHRI C. RAMA-
CHANDRAIAH:
SHRI MANOJ
BHATTACHARYA:
Will the Minister of CONSUMER
AFFAIRS, FOOD AND PUBLIC
DISTRIBUTION be pleased to state:
(a) whether the stock of wheat with
Government agencies has plummeted to an
all-time low barely enough to meet the
stipulated buffer stock norms;
(b) if so, the details thereof; and
(c) the steps proposed to be taken to
augment the wheat stock to ensure food
security and to enable Government to meet
its other commitments?
Disused rail routes/lines in Tamil
Nadu
*86. SHRI T.T.V. DHINAKARAN:
Will the Minister of RAILWAYS be pleased
to state:
(a) the details of railway routes/lines
which are in disuse in Tamil Nadu;
(b) the length of such routes with
railway stations on the routes and the
number of years of disuse of each route;
(c) the reasons for disuse in each case;
and
(d) when the recent assessment of each
route was done to consider operating trains
on these routes?
AIIMS like hospital in Rajasthan
†*87. DR. PRABHA THAKUR: Will
the Minister of HEALTH AND FAMILY
WELFARE be pleased to state:
(a) whether Government have a plan to
set up a hospital in Rajasthan, on the lines
of the All India Institute of Medical Sciences
in Delhi;
(b) if so, whether necessary survey has
been conducted for setting up of hospital
in the State; and
(c) the location in the State where the
said hospital will be set up and expected
cost and capacity fixed for the hospital and

"Total safety" in Railways

Minister of RAILWAYS be pleased to
state:
(a) whether it is a fact that recently some
fresh initiatives have been taken to achieve
"total safety" on the Indian Railways; and
(b) if so, the details thereof including
specific steps contemplated for addressing
the problem of unmanned crossings and

Promoting organic farming
489. SHRI R.S. GAVAI:
SHRI EKANATH K.
THAKUR:
Will the Minister of AGRICULTURE
be pleased to state:
(a) whether it is a fact that India is lagging
behind in expanding organic farming despite
being placed in an advantageous position;
(b) whether it is also a fact that despite
allocating considerable funds for National
Programme for Organic Production in the
current plan, the organic sector lags far
behind its actual potential;
(c) if so, the reasons therefor; and
(d) the steps Government propose to
take to promote organic farming in the
country and also to achieve the target set
out in the plan?
 Research on pest resistance of
Bt. cotton
490. SHRI EKANATH K. THAKUR:
Will the Minister of AGRICULTURE be
pleased to state:
(a) whether, according to a study by
Central Institute for Cotton Research
(CICR), a few years down the line, Bt.
cotton might die a natural death at the hands
of American bollworm, the pest it is
supposed to resist;
(b) whether it is a fact that the CICR
has developed a model that predicts exactly
how many years it would take the
notorious pest to become completely
resistant to Bt. Cotton; and
(c) if so, the steps Government propose
to take to arrest its impending decline?
Sale of spurious Bt. cotton seeds
491. SHRI EKANATH K. THAKUR:
Will the Minis ter of AGRICULTURE be
pleased to state:
(a) whether it is a fact that spurious
seeds of Bt. cotton have flooded the markets
of Gujarat, Maharashtra, Karnataka,
Andhra Pradesh, Madhya Pradesh and
other cotton growing areas of the country;
and
(b) if so, the steps Government propose
to take to check the sale of spurious Bt.
cotton seeds?

112
†Original notice of the question received in Hindi.
 Shortfall in agricultural growth
492. SHRI C. RAMA-
CHANDRAIAH:
SHRI MANOJ
BHATTACHARYA:
Will the Minister of AGRICULTURE
be pleased to state:
(a) whether there has been a shortfall in
agricultural growth in the country during
Eighth and Ninth Plans and the three years
of the Tenth Five Year Plan;
(b) if so, the details thereof;
(c) whether mid-term appraisal of the
Tenth Five Year Plan has also expressed
concern on the stagnated rate of agricultural
growth; and
(d) if so, the action proposed by
Government to boost up the growth rate in
the agriculture sector?
 Production of foodgrains
†493. SHRI JANESHWAR MISHRA:
Will the Minister of AGRICULTURE be
pleased to state:
(a) whether it is a fact that the
production of foodgrains in the current year
is apprehended to decrease in comparison
to the production of the same during the
last year;
(b) if so, the efforts being made to meet
the shortage of foodgrains;
(c) how Government propose to
compensate the losses suffered by farmers;
and
(d) the steps being taken by
Government to prevent recurrence of
shortage of foodgrains in future?
 Scheme for development of
sugarcane
494. SHRI S. ANBALAGAN: Will
the Minister of AGRICULTURE be
pleased to state:
(a) whether Government are
implementing any scheme for the
development of sugarcane and to increase
its productivity;
(b) if so, the salient features thereof;
(c) the amount allocated to Tamil Nadu
during each of the last three years for the
implementation of the scheme and the
results achieved as a result thereof, so far;
and
(d) the future targets fixed for the State
and the steps proposed to be taken by the
Central Government to achieve the target?
 Advisory for cost-effective farm
practices
495. SHRIMATI S.G. INDIRA: Will
the Minister of AGRICULTURE be
pleased to state:
(a) whether it is a fact that Government
had issued an advisory to farmers to save
available soil moisture and use cost-
effective farm practices for the Kharif
sowing season;
(b) if so, the details thereof;
(c) whether Government are also
considering to grant assistance to farmers
for cost-effective farm equipments in the
light of shortfall of rain; and
(d) if so, the details thereof?

113
 Shortage of scientists and
technicians
†496. SHRIMATI MAYA SINGH: Will
the Minister of AGRICULTURE be
pleased to state:
(a) whether it is a fact that research work
in the field of agriculture and horticulture is
getting affected due to shortage of scientists
and technicians in the Indian Council of
Agricultural Research;
(b) if so, the details thereof; and
(c) the reasons for the shortage along
with the details of progress of efforts made
to remove the shortage, till now?
 Integrated dairy development project
for Faizabad and Ambedkar Nagar
